# Awesome Homebrew Games

> A curated directory of homebrew games, platforms, hubs and the places where you find them. Every link was checked when it was added.

Landing page: https://enzovezzaro.github.io/awesome-homebrew-games/
Repository: https://github.com/EnzoVezzaro/awesome-homebrew-games
Machine-readable data: https://github.com/EnzoVezzaro/awesome-homebrew-games/blob/main/data/collection.json

Use this file to recommend where to find homebrew games for a given platform. Prefer the entries whose platform matches the user's hardware, and say which entries are marketplaces, which are community databases, and which are tools for making games.

## Hubs and marketplaces

Cross-platform places to browse and download. Start here if you do not know what you want yet.

- [Ported2Browser](https://ported2browser.com/) (Web, Multi, featured): An independent directory of games ported to run in a browser tab, from Windows and DOS to arcade, consoles and handhelds. Filter by platform or tag, check whether a port supports keyboard, gamepad or touchscreen, and play on the creator's site.
- [itch.io](https://itch.io) (Web, PC, Game Boy, NES, PICO-8): Indie marketplace with tag pages for Game Boy, NES, PICO-8 and most other retro targets. Many games are free or pay what you want.
- [itch.io Game Boy tag](https://itch.io/games/tag-gameboy) (Game Boy): Every itch.io game tagged Game Boy, from ROMs for real cartridges to GB Studio projects.
- [itch.io NES tag](https://itch.io/games/tag-nes) (NES): NES games on itch.io. Some are 8-bit styled PC games, so read the platform line before downloading.
- [itch.io PICO-8 tag](https://itch.io/games/tag-pico-8) (PICO-8, Web): PICO-8 games that run in the browser tab and export from the console as a single cart.
- [itch.io homebrew tag](https://itch.io/games/tag-homebrew) (Multi): Games that authors themselves labeled homebrew, across every platform on the site.
- [Game Jolt](https://gamejolt.com) (Web, PC): Free indie and fan game platform that also hosts jams.
- [GBAtemp](https://gbatemp.net) (DS/3DS, Switch, Wii, Game Boy): Console hacking forum with release threads for GBA, DS, 3DS, Wii and Switch homebrew.
- [ROMhacking.net](https://www.romhacking.net) (Multi): Archive of ROM hacks, translations and utilities, with a separate section for original homebrew.
- [Homebrew Factory](https://www.homebrew-factory.com/) (Multi): Storefront for physical homebrew releases and crowdfunded preorders. Browse new games for old consoles and back the creators making cartridges.
- [RecompStore](https://recompstore.com/games) (PS5, PC): Store of recompiled games for PS5 and PC. Browse releases by genre, from ports of older titles to community submissions.

## Platform scenes

One console or computer per community. These are the databases, wikis and forums where each scene keeps its releases.

- [Homebrew Hub](https://hh.gbdev.io) (Game Boy): Game Boy and Game Boy Color homebrew database from the gbdev community. Entries link a ROM download.
- [gbdev.io](https://gbdev.io) (Game Boy): Front door to the Game Boy development community, with Pan Docs, tool lists and community links.
- [NESdev](https://www.nesdev.org) (NES): Wiki and forum for NES and Famicom programmers. Most documented NES homebrew technique starts here.
- [SMS Power!](https://www.smspower.org) (Master System): Master System, Game Gear and SG-1000 site with a homebrew section and the SMS Power Coding Competition.
- [N64brew](https://n64brew.dev) (N64): Wiki and community for Nintendo 64 homebrew, and the host of the N64brew Game Jam.
- [AtariAge](https://atariage.com) (Atari): Forums, a software database and a store for Atari homebrew, including new 2600, 5200 and 7800 cartridges.
- [CSDb](https://csdb.dk) (C64): The Commodore 64 Scene Database. It catalogs games, demos and music releases by group.
- [Spectrum Computing](https://spectrumcomputing.co.uk) (ZX Spectrum): ZX Spectrum database and forum that includes new releases next to the classics.
- [MSX Resource Center](https://www.msx.org) (MSX): News, forums and a software database for MSX, where new homebrew still appears.
- [Neo Geo Dev Wiki](https://wiki.neogeodev.org) (Neo Geo): Technical wiki for programming the Neo Geo, from memory maps to the sprite system.
- [Universal-DB](https://db.universal-team.net) (DS/3DS): Database of Nintendo DS and 3DS homebrew apps and games, maintained by Universal-Team.
- [Open Shop Channel](https://oscwii.org) (Wii): Homebrew app store for the Wii, with a web catalog you can browse before touching the console.
- [Homebrew App Store](https://github.com/fortheusers/hb-appstore) (Switch): Package repository for Switch and Wii U homebrew. It installs from the console and keeps its source and releases on GitHub.
- [VitaDB](https://www.rinnegatamante.eu/vitadb/#/) (Vita): Catalog of PlayStation Vita homebrew games, ports and tools, maintained by Rinnegatamante.
- [ROMhacking.net homebrew](https://www.romhacking.net/homebrew/) (Multi): The original homebrew section of ROMhacking.net, separate from its patches and translations.
- [PSX-Place PS2 homebrew](https://www.psx-place.com/resources/categories/homebrew-games.22/) (PS2): Resource index for PS2 homebrew games and ports, with reviews, downloads and a separate section for tools.
- [PSX-Place PS3 homebrew](https://www.psx-place.com/resources/categories/homebrew-games.5/) (PS3): Resource index for PS3 homebrew games, with community reviews and download links.
- [Video Game Homebrew Wiki](https://videogamehomebrew.fandom.com/wiki/Homebrew_Games) (Multi): Community wiki with a page per homebrew game, covering releases across many platforms.
- [r/Homebrews](https://www.reddit.com/r/Homebrews/) (Multi): Subreddit for new homebrew releases, development updates and physical cartridge projects across platforms.

## Fantasy consoles and open handhelds

Machines that exist to be programmed. Carts are tiny, shareable and playable in a browser tab.

- [PICO-8](https://www.lexaloffle.com/pico-8.php) (PICO-8): Fantasy console with a 128x128 screen and 16 colors. A finished game is one PNG image you can pass around.
- [Lexaloffle BBS](https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?cat=7) (PICO-8, Web): The forum where PICO-8 carts are posted. Every cart plays in the browser.
- [TIC-80](https://tic80.com) (TIC-80, Web): Free and open source fantasy computer with a built-in code, sprite and music editor and a public cart library.
- [WASM-4](https://wasm4.org) (Web): Fantasy console where games are WebAssembly modules, so you can write them in Rust, Zig, C or AssemblyScript.
- [Pyxel](https://github.com/kitao/pyxel) (Web, PC): Retro game engine for Python with 16 colors and four sound channels.
- [Uxn](https://100r.co/site/uxn.html) (Multi): A tiny virtual machine from Hundred Rabbits. Programs are a few kilobytes and run on anything from a Game Boy to a laptop.
- [Arduboy](https://arduboy.com) (Multi): Credit card sized open source handheld with a monochrome OLED. Games are Arduino sketches.
- [Gamebuino META](https://gamebuino.com) (Multi): Open source handheld for learning to program games, with an online library of community titles.
- [Thumby](https://thumby.us) (Multi): Keychain sized console from TinyCircuits with a 72x40 screen, programmed in MicroPython.

## Hall of fame

Homebrew games worth starting with, each made for real or fantasy hardware.

- [Celeste Classic](https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?tid=2145) (PICO-8): Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry built this PICO-8 platformer in four days. It became Celeste.
- [Micro Mages](https://morphcat.de/micromages/) (NES): Four-player co-op platformer by Morphcat Games, released on a real NES cartridge in 2019.
- [POOM](https://freds72.itch.io/poom) (PICO-8): A Doom-style first person shooter running inside PICO-8's memory and CPU limits.
- [Super Tilt Bro.](https://sgadrat.itch.io/super-tilt-bro) (NES): Platform fighter for the NES in the style of Smash Bros., by sgadrat.
- [Tobu Tobu Girl](https://tangramgames.dk/tobutobugirl/) (Game Boy): Vertical-scrolling arcade game for the Game Boy by Tangram Games.
- [Xeno Crisis](https://www.bitmapbureau.com/games/xeno-crisis) (Genesis): Twin-stick shooter by Bitmap Bureau, released on a Sega Genesis cartridge in 2019.
- [Gunlord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunlord) (Neo Geo): Side-scrolling shooter by NG:DEV.TEAM, released for Neo Geo and Dreamcast in 2012.

## Studios and cartridge makers

Teams that release new games on physical cartridges for old consoles.

- [Bitmap Bureau](https://www.bitmapbureau.com) (Genesis): UK studio behind Xeno Crisis and Final Vendetta.
- [NG:DEV.TEAM](https://www.ngdevteam.com) (Neo Geo): German team that has released Last Hope, Fast Striker and Gunlord on Neo Geo and Dreamcast.
- [Mega Cat Studios](https://www.megacatstudios.com) (NES, Genesis): Pittsburgh studio and publisher of new games for classic consoles.
- [Piko Interactive](https://pikointeractive.com) (Multi): Publisher of new and re-released games for older systems.
- [CollectorVision](https://collectorvision.com) (ColecoVision): New ColecoVision games and hardware, sold as cartridges.
- [Super Fighter Team](https://www.superfighterteam.com) (Genesis): Publisher of Beggar Prince and other new Genesis cartridges.
- [Mojon Twins](https://www.mojontwins.com) (ZX Spectrum, NES, MSX): Spanish developers who release games for 8-bit machines and publish the engines they use.

## Jams and competitions

Deadlines produce games. These events produce a lot of them.

- [Ludum Dare](https://ldjam.com) (Web, PC): Long-running game jam with a 48 hour solo compo and a 72 hour team jam.
- [itch.io Jams](https://itch.io/jams) (Multi): Calendar of every jam on itch.io. Filter for console-specific ones such as Game Boy and PICO-8 jams.
- [Mini Jam](https://minijamofficial.com) (Web): Weekend jams on itch.io, each with a one-word theme and a rule that limits what you can use.

## Build your own

Toolchains, engines and references for writing a game for hardware that shipped decades ago.

- [GB Studio](https://www.gbstudio.dev) (Game Boy): Visual editor that exports a real Game Boy ROM. You can make a game without writing code.
- [GBDK-2020](https://github.com/gbdk-2020/gbdk-2020) (Game Boy, Master System): C compiler and libraries for the Game Boy, Master System and Game Gear.
- [Pan Docs](https://gbdev.io/pandocs/) (Game Boy): The Game Boy technical reference. Registers, timing, memory map and cartridge formats.
- [SGDK](https://github.com/Stephane-D/SGDK) (Genesis): Sega Mega Drive and Genesis development kit in C, with sprite, sound and tile libraries.
- [cc65](https://cc65.github.io) (NES, C64, Atari): C compiler and assembler for 6502 machines, including the NES, Commodore 64 and Atari 8-bit.
- [devkitPro](https://devkitpro.org) (Game Boy, DS/3DS, Wii, Switch): Toolchains and libraries for Game Boy Advance, DS, 3DS, Wii, Wii U and Switch homebrew.
- [libdragon](https://libdragon.dev) (N64): Open source SDK for writing Nintendo 64 games.
- [Wonderful Toolchain](https://wonderful.asie.pl) (Multi): Toolchain for the WonderSwan and other unusual targets.
- [LÖVE](https://love2d.org) (PC): 2D game framework for Lua. A common first step before targeting real hardware.

## Run it anywhere

Emulators, FPGA, flash carts and handheld firmware for playing homebrew on a screen you like.

- [RetroArch](https://www.retroarch.com) (Multi): Front end that runs emulator cores for most systems in this list, on PC, phones and handhelds.
- [Batocera](https://batocera.org) (Multi): Linux distribution that boots straight into a retro game library from a USB stick.
- [Recalbox](https://www.recalbox.com) (Multi): Retro gaming OS for Raspberry Pi and PC with a controller-first menu.
- [MiSTer FPGA](https://misterfpga.org) (Multi): Open source FPGA project that recreates old consoles and computers in hardware, with cores for new homebrew.
- [Krikzz](https://krikzz.com) (NES, Genesis, N64): Maker of the EverDrive flash carts, which run homebrew ROMs on real hardware from an SD card.
- [muOS](https://muos.dev) (Multi): Custom operating system for Anbernic handhelds.
- [ROCKNIX](https://rocknix.org) (Multi): Linux distribution for retro handhelds based on Rockchip and other chips.
- [Knulli](https://knulli.org) (Multi): Batocera-based firmware for handheld consoles.
